correctness.rationale: Root the tree at the seed and pre-sample independent local event sequences at activation. The informed parent stays informed, and an initially ignorant child can first become informed only through its parent. Hence only the parent's own next event changes its count j of informed neighbors while it is active. At count j the next local event is transmission with probability (d−j)/(d−j+α_v j). The root starts at j=0, whose factor is 1, and a nonroot starts at j=1; both stop the success test at j=d. Local success events are functions of disjoint randomness, and induction on the rooted tree identifies their conjunction with full dissemination. For a common α the reciprocal factors with j and d−j pair to (1+αu)(1+α/u)≥(1+α)², strictly for unequal indices. Thus the exponent is sum_v(d_v−1)=n−2 and equality holds exactly for maximum degree at most two. This includes the two-vertex tree, whose product is empty. A separate exact three-state recursion agrees for all seeds on representative shapes and both homogeneous and heterogeneous rates.

Tree structure, permanent informed status, and source-wise rates constant across neighbors are essential to the argument; the path extremum is for a common ratio only.

value.rationale: The full-coverage observable yields an exact finite-tree invariant despite vertex-dependent contact and cessation rates and root-dependent child counts. At common ratio it both collapses the topology to the degree multiset and completely identifies the optimal shape, with strict loss at any branch vertex. This answers a natural seed-choice and topology question that mean-reach and infinite-survival results do not settle.
residual_risks: No extremum for heterogeneous ratios or claim for mean reach or arbitrary networks follows.
